findings.trigger_anchor: const gated = gate.readError !== undefined ? model.provider === "google" : isAgyRouted(model.provider, model.model_id, gate.mode);
findings.cross_file_justification: config.ts (diff-touched) marks every google voice notPlanned whenever readAgyGate reports readError; multi-model-pipeline.ts (diff-touched) then subtracts notPlanned from the required participant count for the merge gate and skips the strict-mode throw for those voices.
findings.description: The agy gate is documented as fail-closed, but its failure mode fails OPEN for the two controls that matter. When `yq` is absent, times out, or `.loa.config.yaml` is malformed, `validateApiKeys` moves every google voice to `notPlanned`. In `executeMultiModelReview` that has two effects: (1) `api_key_mode: "strict"` no longer throws for those voices — it only logs a warn — so a strict-mode operator gets a review with fewer voices than configured; (2) the merge-block invariant (`modelResults.length !== models.length - notPlanned.length`) is satisfied with the reduced set, so a verdict from the remaining voices can clear `mergeBlocked`. A review host missing `yq`, or a repo whose `.loa.config.yaml` is unreadable, therefore lowers the reviewer quorum rather than blocking merge. The pre-change comment states the invariant explicitly: 'Incomplete or degraded participation can never clear a merge.'
findings.failure_mode: A configured 3-voice strict review (anthropic, openai, google) runs on a host without `yq` or with a corrupt `.loa.config.yaml`. The google voice is silently dropped at warn level, strict mode does not fail, and the two remaining voices can produce an APPROVED band that clears `mergeBlocked`. If `repoRoot` ever points at a PR-head checkout, the PR author can trigger this by corrupting `.loa.config.yaml`.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat `gate.readError` as a hard failure for strict mode (throw, as missing keys do) and keep `mergeBlocked = true` whenever `keyStatus.notPlanned` is non-empty due to a read error. Only subtract voices from the required count when the opt-in was read successfully and is explicitly false. Consider also pinning the merge gate to `multiConfig.models.length` and recording not-planned voices as a separate, non-clearing degradation.

findings.description: The agy opt-in that decides whether google voices are dispatched through the Antigravity CLI (spending operator-side CLI auth/quota) or dropped from the review is read from `.loa.config.yaml` under `config.repoRoot`, falling back to the current working directory. This is repository- and cwd-controlled data governing a routing decision, not operator-controlled configuration (env/CLI). The code correctly refuses to let the environment opt IN, but it lets a repo file do so. Whether this is exploitable depends on whether `repoRoot` can ever be a checkout of untrusted PR content; from the diff alone that cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_mode: If the reviewer runs against a checkout containing the PR under review, the PR author can flip `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` to route google voices through the operator's agy CLI session, or set it false / corrupt the file to remove the google reviewer from quorum (see SEC-1).
findings.suggested_fix: Document and enforce that `repoRoot` is the operator's trusted checkout, or read the opt-in from an operator-owned location (e.g. `~/.loa/config.yaml` or an explicit CLI flag) with the repo file as a lower-priority source that can only turn the route OFF.

findings.trigger_anchor: ? `not planned: ${notPlannedList} (the agy gate failed closed: Loa config unreadable — ${agyGate.readError}; hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in)`
findings.cross_file_justification: config.ts captures raw yq stderr / Node error text into `readError`; multi-model-pipeline.ts interpolates it into a thrown Error message and warn logs; main.ts prints it via agyGateStartupLines.
findings.description: `readError` carries the first 300 chars of raw `yq` stderr or the Node spawn error (`spawnSync yq ENOENT`, absolute path of `.loa.config.yaml`, yq parse diagnostics). It is interpolated into the `No models available` Error thrown from `executeMultiModelReview`. If that error text is ever surfaced in a PR comment or run summary rather than only in operator logs, it leaks local filesystem paths and tool inventory of the review host.
findings.failure_mode: An unreadable config causes the pipeline to throw with a message containing the host's absolute config path and yq's raw diagnostic; any caller that posts or persists the error message externally exposes host details.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a short, fixed reason code in `readError` for user-facing strings (e.g. `yq-missing`, `yaml-parse-error`) and log the raw stderr separately at debug level; avoid interpolating raw subprocess stderr into thrown Error messages.

findings.anchor: '{"opt": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | (tag == "!!bool" and . == true)), "canon": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | (tag == "!!bool" and (. == true or . == false))), "tag": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | tag), "mode": (.hounfour.headless.mode // "")}',
findings.description: The `canon` check is dead: once yq has tagged a scalar `!!bool`, `. == true or . == false` is always true, so the 'boolean spelled other than true/false' warning can never fire. Meanwhile yq v4 accepts `True`, `TRUE`, `False` as `!!bool`, so those spellings DO opt in here. The comment claims the bash reader (`lib/agy-gate-lib.sh`) and the Python reader apply the same strict rule; a bash reader doing a literal `== true` match would disagree, producing a gate that plans a google voice in TypeScript which cheval then refuses (or vice versa). The gate is a security-relevant routing decision and the three readers should agree on exactly which inputs opt in.
findings.failure_mode: `agy_opt_in: True` opts in via this reader but may not via the bash gate, so BB dispatches a google voice that cheval rejects (or the reverse), yielding inconsistent planned/not-planned accounting across the pipeline and the quorum math in SEC-1.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the raw scalar text rather than the normalized value, e.g. add `"raw": (.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | tostring)` and require `raw == "true"` in TypeScript; add a parity test that feeds `True`, `yes`, `"true"`, and `true` to all three readers and asserts identical results. Remove the dead `canon` branch.
